surfaces.part: curved bronze rib running down and to the right

answer.evidence: A flat wall-mounted rib piece drawn face-on against a brick wall. The gold cap (rows 2-4) is a small rectangle with a lighter top row (row 2, #dfc872) fading to darker rows below (row 4, #7e5c10). Its outline is dark at row 1 and row 5. It has no front-edge line with eave shadow and no ellipse, so it reads as a lit vertical face, not a horizontal top. The bronze rib below (rows 6-15) is a diagonal strip with highlight and shadow along its length and no horizontal surface. The object reads as a front elevation with no top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: On the measured facts the candidate holds up. It has 15 visible tones per tile against 9-20 for the references, and 0% near-flat coverage, so there are no flat fills. The checkered stone grain gives it some texture. The weak point is structure. The edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, and the stone body reads as a neutral dark grey with a black edge, not a darker tint of the adjacent material. The small brown handle-like element at top left looks like a plain shape with a dark edge. The stone ramp has only about 3-4 distinguishable steps, against 5-6 on the Beodeul references (the roofed well, the cheese stall). Overall it looks closer to a sticker than to the reference craft. Because the edges are neutral and the shading is shallow, I fail it when in doubt.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a single full-bleed 16x16 ceiling tile: a dark stone-like ground with a brown rib or bracket at the top. It has 15 visible tones per tile, against 17 for the cheese stall, 20 for the roofed well and 9 for the hedge, so it is on par and slightly below the richest references. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills, and the ground carries grain and variation. The dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, which on its own would point to a black-line look. The lamp-crook reference measures the same, and the rib is separated mostly by value against the dark ground rather than wrapped in a sticker outline. I therefore call the outline mixed rather than near_black. The stepping is about 5 tones, close to Beodeul's 5-6, so I judge it acceptable next to the references. At this small size the image is hard to read, which limits confidence in the tint call.
